Check the assumptions of the analysis of variance

Source: R/assumptions.R
check_assumptions.Rd

Runs the usual checks on the residuals of a fitted design: normality (Shapiro-Wilk, Anderson-Darling, Jarque-Bera), homogeneity of variances among treatments (Levene with median and with mean, Bartlett, Fligner-Killeen, Hartley's Fmax), additivity of blocks and treatments (Tukey's one-degree-of-freedom test, only for blocked designs), independence in data order (Durbin-Watson) and extreme studentized residuals. The checks are summarised in a grade from A (assumptions satisfied) to D (several assumptions fail).

Usage

check_assumptions(fit, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

fit

An "ad_anova" object from design_anova().

alpha

Significance level of the checks.

Value

An object of class "ad_assumptions" with the table of tests (tests), the residuals and studentized residuals (residuals), the observations with |studentized residual| > 2.5 (suspicious) and the grade.

Details

Each check is rated "ok" when its p-value is at least alpha, "warn" when it lies between alpha / 5 and alpha and "bad" below alpha / 5. The grade is D with two or more "bad" checks, C with one "bad" or two "warn", B with a single "warn" and A otherwise.

Examples

fit <- design_anova(maize_nitrogen, "Yield_t_ha", "Nitrogen_kg_ha", block = "Block")
check_assumptions(fit)
#> 
#> Assumptions of the ANOVA for Yield_t_ha (alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#>  Check        Test                        Statistic    df    p      Rating
#>  normality    Shapiro-Wilk                W = 0.9304         0.2477 ok    
#>  normality    Anderson-Darling            A2 = 0.4947        0.1840       
#>  normality    Jarque-Bera                 JB = 2.303   2     0.3162       
#>  variances    Levene (median)             F = 0.5348   3, 12 0.6672 ok    
#>  variances    Levene (mean)               F = 4.27     3, 12 0.0287       
#>  variances    Bartlett                    K2 = 0.1708  3     0.9822       
#>  variances    Fligner-Killeen             X2 = 1.314   3     0.7259       
#>  variances    Hartley Fmax                Fmax = 1.549                    
#>  additivity   Tukey one-degree-of-freedom F = 0.0548   1, 8  0.8208 ok    
#>  extremes     |studentized residual| > 3  count = 0                 ok    
#>  independence Durbin-Watson (data order)  d = 2.451                 ok    
#> 
#> Observations with |studentized residual| > 2.5:
#>  row group observed fitted studentized
#>   16   180     7.31  7.056       2.646
#> 
#> Grade A. Assumptions satisfied. Proceed with the analysis of variance on this scale.
